newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe government silent on alleged gay rape.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe government silent on alleged gay rape.

text.p: Zimbabwe's government has refused to comment on charges of homosexual rape against ex-president Canaan Banana, but its leading official daily says foreign media are unfairly dragging anti-gay President Robert Mugabe into the affair.
On Friday a weekly newspaper, the Zimbabwe Independent, said it was the alleged rape that should be under investigation, not sexual preferences.

Police on Tuesday announced an investigation into the case which blew up on Monday when a high court judge ruled that allegations by a former bodyguard, who says he was abused by Banana during his five years as his aide de camp, "were probably true".

The aide, Zimbabwean police inspector Jefta Dube, was convicted on Monday of murdering a fellow policeman who goaded him by calling him "Banana's wife". Dube says he was forced into a subservient homosexual relationship by his onetime boss.
Dube's lawyer, Byron Hove, told Reuters his client would sue Banana for damages, saying his alleged behaviour was "gross, callous and cruel abuse of his official position".

Dube was jailed for 10 years on Monday for the 1995 shooting of his fellow officer. He told the court homosexual subjugation by Banana had made him depressive and an alcoholic, and the judge ruled Dube could claim diminished responsibility.

Political analysts said the allegations were likely to embarrass Mugabe, who over the last two years has described gays as perverts "worse than dogs and pigs" and said those who paraded as gays must be lynched.
Banana has not been available for comment, and government officials have uncharacteristically declined to comment.
But the state-controlled Herald newspaper hit out on Thursday at foreign media, accusing them of baying for Mugabe's blood and of unfairly treating Banana, 61, as a criminal.

"Government leadership is suddenly in the dock of the international media and is being accused of hypocrisy for publicly denouncing homosexuality while at the same time protecting gays in its hierarchy," it said in a commentary, adding that the charges against Banana were doubtful.
"It is hypocrisy of the highest order to now question the moral stance of President Mugabe and requiring him to explain himself on the basis of the allegations of a murderer.
"What the foreign media is demanding of him is tantamount to asking him to stop condemning crime because there are criminals in Zimbabwe," the editorial said.

Banana, who retired from his largely ceremonial presidential post in December 1987 after seven years in office, was not called to answer Dube's allegations, but Justice David Bartlett ordered police to investigate the case further.
Dube told the court that Banana first abused him in 1986 after inviting him for dinner at his Harare State House, kissing him as he taught him to dance to ballroom music.
Dube said Banana raped him later that year. He said he later gave in to Banana's advances "out of fear and because I realised nothing was going to happen to him because of his position".
